text: Lucretius's argument that we should not fear posthumous non-existence, because it mirrors the pre-natal non-existence we do not lament, is known as the ___ argument.
explanation: The expected answer is 'symmetry.' Lucretius's symmetry argument in De Rerum Natura III holds that pre-natal and post-mortem non-existence are structurally symmetric periods of non-experience, so fearing only the latter is irrational. Nagel replies that the symmetry is illusory, since death deprives an existing person of goods they could still have had, whereas pre-natal non-existence deprives no one.
